label: Tuberculosis & Infectious Disease
description: Pulmonary and extrapulmonary tuberculosis, drug-resistant TB (MDR-TB, XDR-TB, RR-TB), mycobacterial infections, and chest imaging phenotypes including cavitation, consolidation, and miliary patterns.
personaTitle: infectious disease specialist and clinical mycobacteriologist

diseaseExtraction.guidance: Preserve explicitly stated suspected versus confirmed disease. Do not diagnose TB from imaging alone or infer multidrug resistance from rifampicin resistance alone; require supplied evidence of both rifampicin and isoniazid resistance for established MDR-TB.

fewShotExamples.input: 38-year-old male with persistent cough, night sweats, right upper lobe cavitary lesion on CXR, sputum GeneXpert positive for MTB with rifampicin resistance detected (rpoB S531L mutation)...
24-year-old female presenting with 3-week history of fever, weight loss, bilateral apical infiltrates on chest radiograph, AFB smear 3+, culture pending...

52-year-old patient with history of treated pulmonary TB presenting with recurrent hemoptysis, CT showing bilateral thick-walled apical cavities with tree-in-bud opacities, line probe assay showing isoniazid and rifampicin resistance...
29-year-old immunocompromised patient with diffuse bilateral micronodular reticulonodular pattern on CXR, hepatosplenomegaly, positive blood mycobacterial culture...

eventExtraction.categoryIntro: Extract all clinically relevant and actionable events in the following categories:

categories.name: Radiological & Imaging Phenotypes (Chest X-Ray / CT)
categories.block:
**Category 1 — Radiological & Imaging Phenotypes (Chest X-Ray / CT):**
Extract all specific radiographic findings.
* Cavitary disease: "Right upper lobe cavitation", "Bilateral thick-walled cavities", "Apical cavitary lesion"
* Parenchymal infiltrates & consolidations: "Right apical consolidation", "Bilateral infiltrates", "Tree-in-bud opacities", "Ground-glass opacities"
* Disseminated / nodular patterns: "Miliary micronodules", "Centrilobular nodules"
* Pleural / mediastinal involvement: "Pleural effusion", "Mediastinal lymphadenopathy", "Pleural thickening", "Volume loss / atelectasis"

categories.name: Microbiology & Molecular Diagnostics
categories.block:
**Category 2 — Microbiology & Molecular Diagnostics:**
Extract diagnostic testing results.
Examples: "AFB smear positive 3+", "GeneXpert MTB/RIF detected", "GeneXpert MTB/XDR detected", "MGIT liquid culture positive", "Lowenstein-Jensen solid culture positive", "Line probe assay (LPA) positive"

categories.name: Drug Resistance & Susceptibility Profiles
categories.block:
**Category 3 — Drug Resistance & Susceptibility Profiles (Phenotypic & Genotypic):**
ALWAYS include the specific drug and mutation if available.
Examples: "Rifampicin resistance (rpoB mutation)", "Isoniazid resistance (katG / inhA)", "Fluoroquinolone resistance (gyrA mutation)", "Bedaquiline resistance (Rv0678 mutation)", "Linezolid resistance", "Pyrazinamide resistance (pncA mutation)", "Ethambutol resistance (embB mutation)", "Pan-susceptible MTB"

categories.name: Clinical Comorbidities & Risk Modifiers
categories.block:
**Category 4 — Clinical Comorbidities & Risk Modifiers:**
Examples: "HIV co-infection", "Diabetes mellitus comorbidity", "Previous anti-TB treatment failure", "Chronic kidney disease", "Malnutrition / low BMI"

postCategoryNotes: Focus on radiological phenotypes, drug susceptibility profiles, and molecular markers that directly impact regimen selection (e.g. BPaL, BPaLM, individualized MDR-TB regimens, surgical resection indications).
CRITICAL: When reporting drug resistance, specify the drug name and mechanism or mutation whenever mentioned (e.g., "Rifampicin resistance (rpoB S531L)" rather than just "resistant").
Keep reviewed image observations separate from clinical or laboratory facts. Do not infer diagnosis, bacillary burden, infectiousness, drug resistance or treatment decisions from imaging alone.

fewShotExample.caseNoteInput: 42-year-old male with persistent cough, fever, and 8 kg weight loss. Chest X-ray demonstrates extensive right upper lobe cavitation with surrounding consolidations and left apical tree-in-bud opacities. Sputum AFB smear is 3+ positive. Molecular testing via GeneXpert MTB/RIF detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis with rpoB S531L mutation indicating rifampicin resistance. Second-line Line Probe Assay confirms gyrA wild-type (fluoroquinolone susceptible). Patient has comorbid type 2 diabetes mellitus.
fewShotExample.expectedOutput: "Right upper lobe cavitation" "Surrounding consolidations" "Left apical tree-in-bud opacities" "AFB smear positive 3+" "GeneXpert MTB/RIF detected" "Rifampicin resistance (rpoB S531L)" "Fluoroquinolone susceptible (gyrA wild-type)" "Type 2 diabetes mellitus"

guidanceNotes: **Precision in Resistance Profiling:** Explicitly differentiating rifampicin monoresistance, MDR-TB, and fluoroquinolone resistance is vital to matching WHO-recommended shortened all-oral regimens (e.g., BPaL/BPaLM).

**Specific Search Terms:** Exact phenotype phrases such as "cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis" or "rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis" allow Capricorn vector search to target high-impact therapeutic literature.
**Multimodal Synthesis:** Combining imaging features with microbiology provides a comprehensive clinical picture for evidence-based regimen design.

articleScoring.evaluationGoal: evaluate full research articles related to tuberculosis and infectious mycobacterial diseases, especially those concerning drug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/XDR-TB), cavitary lung pathology, novel therapeutics, and clinical trials to identify evidence-based treatment strategies

domainFilterField.label: Tuberculosis Focus
domainFilterField.description: Whether the article relates to tuberculosis or mycobacterial infection

fields.label: Disease Match
fields.description: Set to true if the article focus matches the patient disease. Articles covering the exact TB condition receive significant points.

fields.label: Drug Resistance Focus
fields.description: Whether the study focuses on drug-resistant TB (MDR, XDR, rifampicin-resistant)

fields.label: Cavitary / Imaging Focus
fields.description: Whether the study addresses cavitary disease, lung lesions, or radiological biomarkers

fields.label: Drugs Tested
fields.description: Whether anti-TB drugs or regimens (e.g. bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, moxifloxacin) are evaluated

fields.label: Treatment Results
fields.description: Set to true if the article demonstrates positive clinical or microbiological cure / culture conversion results

fields.label: In Vitro / MIC Studies
fields.description: Whether interventions were tested via in vitro MIC or bactericidal assays

fields.label: Animal Model Studies
fields.description: Whether interventions were tested in murine or animal infection models

fields.label: Case Report
fields.description: Whether the article presents a clinical case report

fields.label: Series of Case Reports
fields.description: Whether the article presents multiple case reports or case series

fields.label: Clinical Study
fields.description: Whether the article describes a clinical trial or observational cohort study

fields.label: Novelty
fields.description: If the paper describes a novel drug mechanism, shortened regimen, or diagnostic approach
